headline: Your blood pressure is still above goal, and your cardiologist wants you to restart amlodipine at a lower dose after your heart scan showed mild thickening.

followUps.title: Restart amlodipine after confirming the dose
followUps.detail: The cardiologist first said “amlodipine 10” and corrected it to “5 milligrams.” The plan was to take it once a day. Listen to that part of the recording and confirm the dose with your pharmacist or doctor before you restart it.

followUps.title: Check your blood pressure at home
followUps.detail: Start on April 7, 2026. Check your blood pressure every morning and evening for one week.

followUps.title: Send your blood pressure readings
followUps.detail: Lisa can email the readings to your cardiologist. The timing for sending them was not clear.

followUps.title: Arrange your cardiology follow-up
followUps.detail: Your cardiologist wants to see you in late June or early July 2026. No exact date was given.
followUps.when: In three months, so late June or early July

followUps.title: Arrange your visit with Dr. Smith
followUps.detail: Dr. Smith wants to see you in June 2026. Your cardiologist asked you to go to both visits.

instructions.text: Your blood pressure goal is below 130/80, as long as you feel well at that level.
Take amlodipine at the same time each day. Night is fine, and you can take it with atorvastatin.
If your ankles swell again, call your cardiologist or Dr. Smith. Do not stop amlodipine on your own.
If you feel dizzy when you stand up, sit down and let your cardiology team know. This is especially important in the first two weeks.
Call 911 for chest pain, fainting, or a fast, irregular heartbeat.
Avoid cold tablets with decongestants. They can raise your blood pressure.

unchanged.text: Keep taking ramipril 10 milligrams in the morning.
Keep taking atorvastatin 20 milligrams at night.
Keep taking lansoprazole 30 milligrams before breakfast.

openQuestions.text: When should you send your blood pressure readings? Your cardiologist said to check for a week and send them. At the end, you mentioned sending them in three months.
Will you need a heart monitor for the thumping at night?
openQuestions.resolvesWhen: Your cardiologist said to call if the thumping happens more often or feels fast and irregular. The plan then is to have you wear a monitor for a couple of days.
